items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy geography story video for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is thrilled to be telling you this: bursting with energy, a hyped, super-excited host, bright and very expressive, like an excited friend who can't wait to show you something amazing. Big smile in the voice. Wide, lively pitch movement: rise with real curiosity on every question, say every number with a genuine 'WOW', and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. The 'wildest part' line is whispered-excited, like sharing a secret. Speak every word completely and clearly, including short opening words like 'And', 'So' and 'But'; never clip, swallow, stretch or slur a word. The first line ends on a punchy, curious 'Why?'. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Either way, that's why...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy or documentary-serious. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same energy level throughout. Pronounce 'Atherton' as 'ATH-er-tun'.
lines: America's richest town has zero shops. Why?
Meet Atherton, California. Barely five square miles. About seven thousand people.
A typical home here costs ten point seven million dollars.
That's the priciest ZIP code in America. Nine times in eleven years.
So where does all that money go shopping?
Nowhere. No stores. No restaurants. Not even a gas station.
The town's rules allow zero business land.
Most streets don't even have sidewalks.
And a new home needs at least one full acre.
Atherton had a train station for over a hundred and fifty years.
In twenty twenty, it closed. Now trains just pass through.
So why pay ten million dollars to live here?
Look at the map. Stanford is next door. Meta and Google are a short drive away.
It's Silicon Valley's quietest hiding place.
No crowds. No tourists. Just trees and gates.
So... dream town, or just too quiet? Either way, that's why...
